text: In July 2019 a U.S. Department of Labor administrative law judge found that Enterprise RAC Company of Baltimore (a wholly-owned Enterprise Holdings subsidiary) unlawfully discriminated against African-American applicants for its management trainee program in fiscal 2007-2012 and 2014-2017.
short: 2019 DOL ALJ hiring-discrimination finding against Enterprise's Baltimore subsidiary

source.name: OFCCP v. Enterprise RAC Company of Baltimore, LLC — Administrative Law Judge Recommended Findings and Order, July 17, 2019 (copy hosted by Roffman Horvitz PLC)
source.quote: The statistical and anecdotal evidence established a prima facie case that Defendant unlawfully discriminated against African-American applicants for its management trainee program
source.note: Recommended Findings no. 3, page 122; the decision also orders job offers to 182 class members. The same document stipulates (Conclusions of Law no. 3): 'Enterprise is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Enterprise Holdings, Inc.' The original on dol.gov blocks scripts, so this law-firm copy of the decision text is cited. A second publisher describes the order: see additionalSources.

additionalSources.name: Automotive Fleet: Enterprise Ordered to Pay Over $6M in Race Discrimination Case
additionalSources.quote: ordered by a federal judge to pay over $6.6 million in back wages and benefits to more than 2,300 black applicants who were rejected by the federal contractor’s management trainee program
additionalSources.note: Same article: 'the applicants were turned down because of their race. It’s the largest back wages award ever under the Department of Labor’s federal contract compliance program.'
